original_value: Timely and accurate soil moisture information is of great importance in agricultural monitoring. The Gaofen-3 (GF-3) satellite, the first C-band multi-polarization synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) satellite in China, provides valuable data sources for soil moisture monitoring. In this study, a soil moisture retrieval algorithm was developed for the GF-3 satellite based on a backscattering coefficient simulation database. We adopted eight optical vegetation indices to determine the relationships between these indices and vegetation water content (VWC) by combining Landsat-8 data and field measurements. A backscattering coefficient database was built using an advanced integral equation model (AIEM). The effects of vegetation on backscattering coefficients were corrected using the water cloud model (WCM) to obtain the bare soil backscattering coefficient (     σ  s o i l  °     ). Then, soil moisture retrievals were obtained at HH, VV and HH+VV combination respectively by minimizing the observed bare soil backscattering coefficient (     σ  s o i l  °     ) and the AIEM-simulated backscattering coefficient (     σ  soil-simu  °     ). Finally, the proposed algorithm was validated in agriculture region of wheat and corn in China using ground soil moisture measurements. The results showed that the normalized difference infrared index (NDII) had the best fit with measured VWC values (R = 0.885) among the eight vegetation water indices; thus, it was adopted to correct the effects of vegetation. The proposed algorithm using GF-3 satellite data performed well in soil moisture retrieval, and the scheme combining HH and VV polarization exhibited the highest accuracy, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.044 m3m−3, followed by HH polarization (RMSE = 0.049 m3m−3) and VV polarization (RMSE = 0.053 m3m−3). Therefore, the proposed algorithm has good potential to operationally estimate soil moisture from the new GF-3 satellite data.

result.paraphrase: Timely, accurate soil moisture information is highly important for agricultural monitoring. China’s Gaofen-3 (GF-3), the country’s first C-band multi-polarization synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) satellite, offers valuable data for soil moisture monitoring. In this study, a soil moisture retrieval algorithm for GF-3 was developed using a backscattering coefficient simulation database. Eight optical vegetation indices were used, together with Landsat-8 data and field measurements, to determine their relationships with vegetation water content (VWC). An advanced integral equation model (AIEM) was employed to build the backscattering coefficient database. Vegetation effects on backscattering coefficients were then corrected with the water cloud model (WCM) to derive the bare soil backscattering coefficient (σsoil°). Soil moisture retrievals were finally obtained for HH, VV, and HH+VV combinations by minimizing the difference between the observed bare soil backscattering coefficient (σsoil°) and the AIEM-simulated backscattering coefficient (σsoil-simu°). The proposed algorithm was validated in wheat and corn agricultural regions in China using ground soil moisture measurements. Among the eight vegetation water indices, the normalized difference infrared index (NDII) showed the best agreement with measured VWC values (R = 0.885) and was therefore used to correct vegetation effects. The GF-3-based algorithm performed well in soil moisture retrieval, and the HH+VV polarization combination achieved the best accuracy, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.044 m3m−3, followed by HH polarization (RMSE = 0.049 m3m−3) and VV polarization (RMSE = 0.053 m3m−3). These results suggest good potential for operational soil moisture estimation from the new GF-3 satellite data.
